title: Rosalind and the Will
premise: When Sable Fairweather supervises the exhumation of town founder Edmund Rosalind for a property dispute, they find the coffin empty — and a fresh will, dated after his death, hidden in the casket lining. The discovery reopens the thirty-year-old case of Rosalind's disappearance, which Sable's late mentor closed as a simple burial. As Sable digs into forged documents, a secret second family, and the mentor's own signature on the falsified death certificate, they realize the founder may have staged his own death to escape a life he no longer wanted. The trial forces Sable to choose between protecting their mentor's legacy and telling the truth: in the end, Sable testifies that Rosalind lived out his days quietly as a gardener two towns over, closing the case at last by honoring both the law and the man's wish to be someone new.
about_author: Xanthe Blackwood is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing county death records before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about the quiet violence of secrets kept too long.

chapters.title: The Grave That Knew Its Own
chapters.summary: Sable Fairweather's POV. Establishing chapter: Sable walks the cemetery at dawn, greeting graves like old friends, then receives the court order to exhume founder Edmund Rosalind. The emotional beat is pride in an unblemished record — and a flicker of unease about disturbing the town's most sacred grave.

chapters.title: Empty Linen, Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The exhumation draws half the town; when the coffin opens, it holds only weighted linen. Sable must formally log an impossible finding while the Rosalind heirs watch, furious. Emotional beat: professional composure cracking into dread as Sable realizes every record says this body was buried thirty years ago.

chapters.title: A Will in the Lining
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Examining the coffin, Sable finds a sealed envelope stitched into the lining: a handwritten will, dated four years after Rosalind's official death, leaving everything to an unknown beneficiary, 'M. Vale.' Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling into isolation as the town begins whispering that Sable has desecrated a legend.

chapters.title: Everyone Swore It Was Closed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, with flashback. Sable rereads the original case file and finds their beloved mentor, Coroner Ada Marsh, signed the death certificate — yet the embalming records are missing. Emotional beat: loyalty at war with doubt; Sable remembers Ada teaching them never to close a case they can't feel in their bones.

chapters.title: The Heirs Arrive
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and heir Julian Rosalind. The family demands the will be declared fraudulent; Julian privately admits he never believed his grandfather's body was in the ground. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming between investigator and suspect, each hiding what they already know.

chapters.title: M. Vale
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Tracing the beneficiary, Sable finds a 'Miriam Vale' who received anonymous payments for decades — and a photograph of Rosalind with a woman who was not his wife. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt shadowed by guilt, since exposing Miriam means exposing a life built on a lie.

chapters.title: What Ada Kept
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Searching Ada Marsh's preserved office, Sable finds a locked drawer and, inside, a second copy of the will plus a note in Ada's hand: 'He asked me to let him go. I did.' Emotional beat: grief and betrayal braided together — the mentor Sable worshipped broke the law out of compassion.

chapters.title: Trial Notice
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The estate dispute escalates into a formal hearing challenging the death certificate itself, meaning Sable must testify. Julian weighs whether protecting the family name matters more than truth. Emotional beat: pressure mounting from all sides; the clock starts ticking.

chapters.title: The Gardener of Millbrook
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following the payment trail, Sable travels to Millbrook and finds an old groundskeeper, 'Edmund Vale,' recently deceased — buried under a modest stone. Emotional beat: quiet devastation; Sable stands at the real grave of the man everyone thought they knew.

chapters.title: Miriam
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Sable and elderly Miriam Vale. She confirms everything: Edmund faked his death to escape a marriage of ambition and start over with her. She begs Sable to leave him in peace. Emotional beat: tenderness against duty — Sable sees, painfully, the love story inside the crime.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession, Unsent
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. A letter Ada wrote but never mailed reveals she helped stage the death because Edmund was dying anyway and begged to spend his last years free. Emotional beat: Sable confronts the question at the heart of the book — was Ada's lie mercy or corruption?

chapters.title: Someone Else Knows
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable discovers the will's existence leaked before the exhumation — someone tipped off Julian's lawyer. Someone else has known for years. Emotional beat: paranoia; the mystery pivots from 'what happened' to 'who is pulling strings now.'

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Ledger
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian investigates his own attorney, Harrow, and finds payments from a rival branch of the family who'd inherit nothing if the will stood. Emotional beat: disillusionment — Julian realizes his righteous fury was weaponized.

chapters.title: Threats in the Archive
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable's office is broken into; the original file pages on Ada's certificate go missing. A warning note appears: 'Some graves stay shut.' Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve — Sable refuses to be frightened off the one case that defines them.

chapters.title: Two Truths Before the Bench
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Pre-trial deposition: opposing counsel traps Sable into admitting Ada falsified records. Sable must decide mid-testimony how much truth serves justice. Emotional beat: the cost of honesty made concrete; Sable chooses partial truth and hates themselves for it.

chapters.title: What Edmund Wanted
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV. Miriam gives Sable Edmund's final letter, written on his deathbed: he asked that the will stand, not for money, but so the town would finally know he chose to leave. Emotional beat: Sable stops seeing a fugitive and sees a man claiming his own identity at last.

chapters.title: Harrow's Move
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Harrow moves to have the will suppressed and Sable discredited, revealing he's known about the empty coffin for a decade and stayed silent for payment. Emotional beat: outrage uniting Sable and Julian openly as allies.

chapters.title: The Night Before Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable visits Ada's grave and reads her the letter she never sent, deciding to tell the whole truth tomorrow regardless of consequence. Emotional beat: stillness and acceptance; the theme of memory versus identity crystallizes.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Climax: Sable testifies to everything — the empty coffin, the staged death, Ada's mercy, Harrow's blackmail — placing truth above legacy and career. Emotional beat: catharsis through confession; Sable closes the case everyone swore was closed by finally opening it fully.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. The judge upholds the will; Harrow faces charges; the family, shaken, chooses reconciliation over appeal. Julian visits both graves — the empty one and the true one — and leaves flowers at each. Emotional beat: mourning a grandfather he never really had, and meeting him for the first time.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Resolution: Sable adds Edmund Vale's true grave to their dawn walk, speaking his real name aloud for the first time. The town slowly forgives; some don't. Emotional beat: peace earned through truth — Sable's record remains unblemished because they learned which cases deserve to be reopened.

chapters.title: The Will of Rosalind
chapters.summary: Miriam's POV, epilogue. Miriam donates Edmund's letters to the town archive, letting his full story — founder, husband, runaway, lover — finally coexist in one place. Emotional beat: gentle closure on the themes of memory and identity; a life is remembered whole at last.
